spots.name: City of Arts and Sciences

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The City of Arts and Sciences is a cultural and architectural complex in the city of Valencia, Spain. It is the most important modern tourist destination in the city of Valencia and one of the 12 Treasures of Spain.

spots.name: Lonja de la Seda
spots.summary: The Lonja de la Seda ; or Llotja de la Seda (Valencian: [ˈʎɔdʒa ðe la ˈseða]; or alternatively in English "Silk Exchange", is a late Valencian Gothic-style civil building in Valencia, Spain. It is a principal tourist attraction in the city.

spots.name: Valencia Cathedral
spots.summary: Valencia Cathedral, at greater length the Metropolitan Cathedral–Basilica of the Assumption of Our Lady of Valencia, also known as St Mary's Cathedral, is a Catholic church in Valencia, Spain.

spots.name: Palace of the Marqués de Dos Aguas

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of the Marquis of Dos Aguas is a Rococo nobility palace, historically important in the city. It is located in one of the most central locations in the city of Valencia (Spain). It is a stately mansion that was the property of the Marqueses of Dos Aguas and is currently owned by the Spanish State.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Palace of the Marqués de Dos Aguas

spots.name: Torres de Serranos
spots.summary: The Serrans Gate or Serranos Gate, also known as Serrans Towers or Serranos Towers is one of the twelve gates that formed part of the ancient city wall, the Christian Wall, of the city of Valencia, Spain. It was built in Valencian Gothic style at the end of the 14th century.

spots.name: El Micalet
spots.summary: The Miguelete Tower is the bell tower of the Valencia Cathedral in Valencia, Spain. It is known as El Miguelete in Castilian Spanish or Torre del Micalet in the Valencian language. Construction of the tower began in 1381 and was completed in 1429.

spots.name: Plaça de l'Ajuntament
spots.summary: The modernization of the Plaza de Emilio Castelar was designed by municipal architect Francisco Javier Goerlich from 1927, with the main reform carried out between 1931 and 1933. It later became the Plaza of the City Hall and its fountain.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Modernisme Plaza of the City Hall of Valencia

spots.name: Mercat Central

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Mercado Central or Mercat Central is a public market located across from the Llotja de la Seda and the Church of Santos Juanes in central Valencia, Spain. It is one of the main works of the Valencian Art Nouveau.

spots.name: L'Oceanogràfic
spots.summary: L'Oceanogràfic is an oceanarium situated in the Garden of the Turia to the southeast of the city center of Valencia, Spain, where different marine habitats are represented. It was designed by the architect Félix Candela and the structural engineers Alberto Domingo and Carlos Lázaro.

spots.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Forsaken

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Basilica of Our Lady of the Forsaken is located in the city of Valencia, Spain. It is the sanctuary of the Lady of the Forsaken, Patron Saint of Valencia and of the entire Old Kingdom of Valencia, current Valencian Community. It holds the dignity of a basilica thanks to the papal brief signed by SS.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of Our Lady of the Forsaken

spots.name: Torres de Quart
spots.summary: The Torres de Quart or Puerta de Quart is one of the two remaining gates of the old Valencia city wall. It was built between 1441 and 1493. It was still in use during the Peninsular War when it was marked by cannonballs and musket shots.

spots.name: Plaça de la Mare de Déu
Estació del Nord
spots.summary: The Estació del Nord (Valencian), or Estación del Norte (Spanish), both meaning "North Station", is the major railway station in Valencia, Spain. It is located in the city centre next to the Plaça de Bous or Plaza de Toros, the city's bullring, and 200 metres from the town hall.

spots.name: San Nicolás, Valencia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Church of Sant Nicolau de Bari and Sant Pere Màrtir is a Valencian Gothic style, Catholic parish church located in Valencia, Spain.

spots.name: Museu de les Ciències Príncipe Felipe
spots.summary: The Museu de les Ciències Príncipe Felipe is a science museum in Valencia, Spain. It is part of the City of Arts and Sciences, an architectural complex within the city, and can be found at the end of Luis García Berlanga Street. Its director is Manuel Toharia, a Spanish science writer and television personality.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museu de les Ciències Príncipe Felipe

spots.name: Museu de Belles Arts de València

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museu de Belles Arts de València is an art gallery in Valencia, Spain, founded in 1913. It houses some 2,000 works, most dating from the 14th–17th centuries, including a Self portrait of Diego Velázquez, a St. John the Baptist by El Greco, Goya's Playing Children, Gonzalo Pérez's Altarpiece of Sts.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museu de Belles Arts de València

spots.name: Palace of the Generalitat Valenciana

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of the Generalitat Valenciana, is a historic palace dating from the 15th century, initially built in the Valencian Gothic style with later Renaissance additions and changes. Today, it houses the offices of the executive of the Generalitat Valenciana.

spots.name: Plaza de Toros de Valencia
spots.summary: Plaza de Toros de Valencia, officially Plaça de Bous de València, is a bullring in Valencia, Spain. It was built between 1850 and 1859 in the neoclassical style, inspired by civil Roman architecture such as the Colosseum in Rome or the Arena of Nîmes (France).

spots.name: Santa Catalina, Valencia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Catherine's Church is a Gothic-style Catholic church located in the city of Valencia, Spain at the southern end of Plaza de la Reina.

spots.name: Casa de los Gatos

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Casa de los Gatos or Casa dels Gats is an animal shelter in Valencia, Spain. Its house-shaped facade was made by artist Alfonso Yuste Navarro in 2003.

spots.name: Church of Santos Juanes, Valencia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Santos Juanes or Sant Joan del Mercat is a Catholic church located in the Mercat neighborhood of the city of Valencia, Spain.

spots.name: Plaza de la Reina
spots.summary: Plaza de la Reina is a central plaza in Valencia, Spain. It brings together, among others, Calle de la Paz, Calle del Mar, Calle del Cabilleros, Calle de los Bordadores, Calle de Santa Catalina, and Calle de Santo Vincente Mártir.

spots.name: González Martí National Museum of Ceramics and Decorative Arts
spots.summary: The National Museum of Ceramics and Decorative Arts González Martí is a museum in Valencia, Spain, devoted to ceramics –with special importance to Valencian ceramics, porcelains and other decorative arts such as textile art, traditional costumes, and furniture.
spots.wikipediaTitle: González Martí National Museum of Ceramics and Decorative Arts

spots.name: Institut Valencià d'Art Modern

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Institut Valencià d'Art Modern, also known by the acronym IVAM, was the first center of modern art in Spain, opening in 1989 in the city of Valencia. The Institut Valencià d'Art Modern is an important center for modern and contemporary art in Spain and Europe.

spots.name: Turia Garden
spots.summary: The Turia Garden is a public urban park located in the former riverbed of the Turia River in the city of Valencia, Spain. The park spans approximately 136 hectares, with plans to expand to 160.5 hectares in the future.

spots.name: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía
spots.summary: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía is an opera house, performing arts centre, and urban landmark designed by Santiago Calatrava to anchor the northwest end of the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia, Spain. It opened on 8 October 2005; its first opera staging was of Beethoven's Fidelio on 25 October 2006.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía

spots.name: Valencian Museum of Ethnology

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Valencian Museum of Ethnology is a museum located in the city of Valencia, mediterranean Spain. The museum mission defines it as cultural institution primarily devoted to collect, research and communicate the tangible and intangible heritage related to traditional and popular Valencian culture.

spots.name: Warrior of Mogente
spots.summary: Warrior of Moixent is a figure that represents a warrior sitting on a horse. The figure is made out of cast bronze. Warrior of Moixent is from the 5th century or 4th century BCE. The figure was found in 1931, close to Moixent, Spain. Warrior of Moixent is located at Prehistory Museum of Valencia.

spots.name: L'Umbracle

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: L'Umbracle, part of the City of Arts and Sciences complex in Valencia, Spain, is a sculpture garden and landscaped walk with plant species indigenous to Valencia. It harbors in its interior The Walk of the Sculptures, an outdoor art gallery with sculptures from contemporary artists.

spots.name: Valentia Edetanorum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Valencia, known officially in Valencian as València, is the capital and largest city of the Valencian Community and the province of the same name in Spain. It is located on the banks of the Turia, on the east coast of the Iberian Peninsula on the Mediterranean Sea.

spots.name: Centre Arqueològic de l'Almoina
spots.summary: This Visigothic chapel has on display objects discovered during its excavation including a Visigothic altar, Roman mural, Muslim artifacts, and a sculpture of the early Christian Saint Vicente Mártir, who is believed to have been buried here.

spots.name: Valencia City Hall
spots.summary: Valencia City Hall is the seat of local government in Valencia, Spain. It was declared a Bien de Interés Cultural in 1962.

spots.name: Prehistory Museum of Valencia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Prehistory Museum of Valencia is a museum of the city of Valencia, in Spain, that exposes archaeological materials covering from Paleolithic to the Visigoths period.

spots.name: Assut de l'Or Bridge
spots.summary: The Assut de l'Or Bridge is a white single-pylon cable-stayed bridge in the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia, Spain, designed by Valencian architect and civil engineer Santiago Calatrava and completed in December 2008.

spots.name: San Esteban, Valencia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Stephen's Church is a Catholic parish church located in the Plaça de Sant Esteve in the city of Valencia, Valencian Community, Spain.

spots.name: Palace of the Borgias

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of Benicarló is an aristocratic palace of Valencian Gothic and Renaissance styles located in the city of Valencia, Spain. It is now the headquarters of the Valencian Parliament.

spots.name: Real Colegio Seminario del Corpus Christi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Real Colegio Seminario del Corpus Christi is a former Roman Catholic school and seminary founded in 1583 in the Spanish city of Valencia. It is located in calle de la Nau in the old city, opposite La Nau, the former Universidad Literaria.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Real Colegio Seminario del Corpus Christi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Monestir de Sant Miquel dels Reis

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Founded in the 16th century, this massive Renaissance building is considered by some historians to be the early model for the more well-known El Escorial near Madrid. In 1835 the monastery was dissolved and came under control of the state; it was used for a time as a school, an asylum, and during the Franco period as a prison. It was fully restored in 1997-2000, and now houses the central library

spots.name: Convent of Santo Domingo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Convent of Santo Domingo was a convent of the Dominican Order in the city of Valencia, Spain. Construction of the church began on land granted by King James I of Aragon in 1239, but it was subsequently replaced by a larger structure in 1250.

spots.name: Museu del Patriarca

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Managed by the Seminary of Corpus Christi, this museum has a small collection of paintings from the 16th and 17th centuries, with special highlights including works by Juan de Juanes, El Greco, and early Flemish masters. The collection can only be viewed with a tour, offered in a number of European languages; to be sure there is a tour in your language it is best to reserve ahead, either by phone

spots.name: Mercado de Colón
spots.summary: Mercado de Colón or Valencian: Mercat de Colom is a public market located in the city center of Valencia, Spain. It is one of the main works of the Valencian Art Nouveau.

spots.name: Plaça Redona
spots.summary: La Plaça Redona, also called Plaça del Clot is a plaza located in the El Mercat(ca) section of the Ciutat Vella district of Valencia, Spain. It lies in the middle of the triangle formed by three nearby plazas: La Plaça del Mercat, La Plaça de la Reina, and La Plaça de l'Ajuntament.

spots.name: Mestalla Stadium
spots.summary: Mestalla Stadium is a football stadium in Valencia, Spain. The stadium is the home of Valencia CF and has a capacity of 49,430 seats, making it the 8th-largest stadium in Spain, and the largest in the Valencian Community.

spots.name: Jardins del Real de València
spots.summary: Established by the Moors in the 13th century as gardens for the royal palace (no longer standing), this pleasant and popular park is the second-largest park in Valencia, after the Turia gardens. The park includes a rose garden, sculpture garden, bicycle track, and aviary. During the summer various festivals are held here.

spots.name: Almodí de València

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Constructed in the early 14th century on the site of a Moorish palace, the building is essentially Moorish in design and used to function as the municipal granary; its name is derived directly from 'almud' (Arabic: bushel). The building was fully restored in 1996 and is now a venue for temporary art exhibitions.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: El Cabanyal
spots.summary: El Cabanyal (Cabanyal-Canyamelar) is a neighbourhood in the city of Valencia which is part of the sea village. It is located in the eastern part of the city, very near to La Malvarrosa, Valencia's main beach.

spots.name: Del Real Palace, Valencia

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The now demolished Del Real Palace or Royal Palace was the former residence of the kings of Valencia in the «Cap i Casal» of the kingdom, as the city of Valencia was then called. It was on the left bank of the Turia River, where nowadays Jardines del Real are.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Monument to James I
spots.summary: Jaume I or the Monument to James I is an instance of public art in Valencia, Spain. The monument is topped by an equestrian bronze statue representing James I of Aragon, conqueror of Valencia in 1238 and founder of the Kingdom of Valencia.

spots.name: Pont de l'Exposició
spots.summary: Designed by Santiago Calatrava and built between 1991 and 1995, the bridge resembles a comb, hence the nickname 'La Peineta'.

spots.name: Natural Science Museum of Valencia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Natural Science Museum of Valencia (Spain) is located at Jardines del Real.

spots.name: Banys de l'Almirall

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Although constructed in 1313 after the Christian reconquista, the bathhouse was built in the Arabic style and is considered to be an excellent example of Moorish architecture. It was used continuously as a bathhouse until the 20th century, and is one of the few remaining such structures in Spain. It was fully restored in 2005.

spots.name: Museu Valencià de la Il·lustració i de la Modernitat

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The museum is devoted to civics and culture, with special exhibits focused on such topics as graphic design, photography, and cinema. The building and garden were designed by Valencian architect Guillermo Vázquez Consuegra.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Casa-Museu Benlliure

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: This was once home to two generations of the Benlliure family, headed by prominent Valencian artist José Benlliure. The early 20th-century residence has been maintained in three distinct sections, including the primary house with original furnishings and artworks, a lovely courtyard and garden, and a second building with a private study and more artworks.

spots.name: Galería del Tossal

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: This unique underground gallery has been designed around the remains of a city wall from the Moorish period, complete with arches. The gallery is a venue for temporary exhibits of Spanish and international contemporary art.

spots.name: Casa de les Roques

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The horse-drawn carriages used in the Corpus Christi parades, known as roques (Spanish: rocas, or 'rocks'), have been stored in this building since the mid-15th century. Eleven carriages are on display, the oldest of which was built between 1373 and 1392. Other items exhibited are costumes and historic documents, as well as a 25-minute video about the processions (in Spanish).

spots.name: Casa de Sant Vicent Ferrer
spots.summary: Sant Vicent Ferrer, the principal patron saint of Valencia, was born in this house in 1350. The house was renovated numerous times, and has a chapel, well, and 18th-century ceramic tile panels depicting the life of the saint.

spots.name: Fundación Bancaja
spots.summary: The former 19th-century residence is a cultural centre which hosts excellent, well-curated temporary exhibits of contemporary art and photography, by Valencian, Spanish and international artists.

spots.name: Pont de la Trinitat
spots.summary: The oldest bridge in the city, with the current structure dating to the early 16th century. The two 17th-century sculptures of Valencian saints used to be on another nearby medieval bridge, and were relocated to this bridge in the mid-20th century.

spots.name: Palau de Cervelló

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Built in the 18th century as the residence of the counts of Cervelló, this palace became the official residence for visiting royalty following the demolition of the Palau Reial de València. The building now houses a museum, the Municipal Archive, and the Serrano Morales Library. On the ground floor is an exhibit (in Catalan and Spanish) illustrating the historic events which took place here, and o

spots.name: Fundación Chirivella Soriano

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: This well-preserved 14th-century Gothic palace houses a permanent collection of contemporary Spanish art, with rotating exhibits.

spots.name: L'Àgora
spots.summary: A multi-use covered plaza, designed for sporting events, concerts, and special exhibits.

photo.author: Marja van Bochove from The Hague, Netherlands

spots.name: Museo Histórico Militar de Valencia
spots.summary: Built in 1898 for an infantry regiment, the building now houses a collection of over 3,000 objects, most of them from the 19th and 20th centuries.

spots.name: Bombas Gens Centre d'Art

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: This former factory from the 1930s has been transformed into an exhibition space for Spanish contemporary art, with a special focus on photography. The building has an interesting history, as it was used to make industrial pumps, and later during the Spanish Civil War was used by the Republicans as an air raid shelter and to assemble armaments.

spots.name: Drassanes del Grau

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: These Gothic shipyards date to the early 14th century, and attained their current layout in 1500. Trade ships were built and repaired here, as well as galleys used for defense against Barbary pirates. Later the building was used as a storehouse for salt, and now functions as a venue for temporary exhibits.
